source_note: 三向实拍交叉核对。主图取南侧可见的两岸主梯、短临河踏步、矩形石梁孔，不表现全桥所有背面分岔。去除遮挡梁孔的藤蔓与周围民居，保留少量河岸提示。初稿误添第三段长梯已弃用；最终稿改为所选实拍可见的两段主梯。输入与最终输出均已目视检查。
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Create ONE fine-line drawing for the Chinese heritage collection 访古. Image1 is STYLE ONLY: the original Longmen Vairocana delicate organic outline drawing. Images2,3,4 are ACTUAL GEOMETRY of the same BAZI BRIDGE 八字桥 at Shaoxing, Zhejiang. Image2 southeast view is the main composition. Image3 north view and image4 winter northwest view clarify the real stone lintel and stair junctions. Do not copy the Buddha into this bridge.
Render a quiet, refined, sparse BLACK INK drawing on PURE WHITE. Fine confident natural contour lines, selected finer inner structure, all surfaces white. No solid shadow, gray wash, hatching, stippling, dense stone texture, heavy black blocks or engraving. The background becomes transparent and the ink receives the site's dynasty color later. No text, labels, watermark, frame, gold, color or gradient.
CRITICAL SUBJECT GEOMETRY: Baziqiao is a STONE BEAM BRIDGE, NOT a rounded arch bridge. Preserve the SHORT HORIZONTAL stone-lintel span across a nearly RECTANGULAR main canal opening, with vertical stone abutments and very slight actual camber of the top deck. There is NO semicircular arch ring and NO pointed arch. From the southeast main photo, the river runs from the bridge toward the viewer through the CENTER. The bridge spans from LEFT BANK to RIGHT BANK in the rear. Its two long approach stair flights run FORWARD along the two sides of the river toward the viewer, joining the transverse raised deck at the far end. This is a staggered water-street junction, not a single symmetric arched hump with stairs extending in opposite directions on one straight line. Only TWO LONG stair flights are visible from image2, ONE on each bank. Do NOT add a third long stair flight beside the left one. Do NOT combine the opposite-view stairs from images3 and4 into extra stairs in this view: those photos show the SAME bridge from the OTHER SIDE. Keep only the short THREE-TO-FOUR STEP river landing at the foreground left canal edge, which is lower than the long main stairs, without a tall parapet. Preserve this actual lower-bank junction. Preserve the actual flat stone parapets with rectangular open bays, capped stone posts, the curled stone end panels where visible, and the parallel smooth narrow stone ramp strips on the main stair flights. Actual lower stone abutment and canal edges are part of the structure. Retain enough shallow natural perspective to distinguish each stair direction. Do NOT force the crossing into a flattened front elevation or invent unseen symmetrical branches. Choose the southeast view of image2, slightly higher only if necessary for clear stair reading. Remove hanging ivy to reveal the stone lintel and abutment contours confirmed by images3 and4; do not convert the plant curtain into a masonry arch.
Show the COMPLETE main beam bridge, the two visible main approach stair flights, the short low river landing, and a few short canal-bank/water lines. Remove all houses, laundry, people, boats, bikes, trees and ivy. Keep only immediate stone abutments, no elaborate neighboring town scene. Reduce stone blocks to a few chosen masonry joints and steps to light individual tread contours; no tiny cracks, stone mottling, water reflection or dense paving grid. Leave canal opening WHITE, indicated only by lintel and vertical jamb outlines. No black hole. No roof, pavilion or invented arch.
Landscape1536x1024, isolated bridge composition about82%width and65%height, generous clean white margins, all stair ends and railing ends uncut. Beautiful thin sparse line character and blank-space balance consistent with image1.
Final geometry check before rendering: image2 is the exact southeast composition: ONE long stair at left and ONE long stair at right, both running from nearer foreground to far bridge, a horizontal lintel joining their top landings. No third long stair flight, no duplicated left staircase, no speculative symmetrical extra flights. Preserve the real relative spacing and low river landing. The main reference is NOT an exploded view. Use slightly oblique nearfrontal perspective of this actual southeast photograph. Two approach stair flights and only these two.

historical_sources.title: 《绍兴县志（一）》名胜古迹：八字桥
historical_sources.publisher: 浙江省地方志工作办公室·浙江通志
historical_sources.evidence: 始建南宋嘉泰以前，宝祐四年（1256）冬重建、乾隆四十八年（1783）重修。桥为石梁桥，主孔净跨4.5米；位于三条街、三条河交汇，桥梁并列、桥面中间微拱，桥下设纤道。名称源于形如八字。

site_recommendation.name: 八字桥
site_recommendation.sub: 三街三河 · 石梁古桥
site_recommendation.yearNote: 1256为地方志所载重建年，另有1783年重修；今日所见含历代修缮，不表示每块石构件均为1256年原件。
site_recommendation.lede: 石阶沿着河岸升起，在水路上方交汇。八字桥用一孔石梁与几向踏步，接住了绍兴古城交错的街巷和河流。

facts.label: 宝祐重建
facts.text: 桥始建于南宋嘉泰以前，宝祐四年（1256）冬重建，清乾隆四十八年再修。

facts.label: 石梁跨河
facts.text: 主桥以石梁并列跨越水道，主孔净跨约4.5米；矩形梁孔与圆拱桥形制不同。

facts.label: 三街三河
facts.text: 桥处三条街、三条河交错处，石阶向不同方向衔接街岸，名称取自形如八字的布局。
